sections.content: The Ibizan Hound is an elegant, athletic, and intelligent breed known for its incredible speed and keen hunting instincts. Originally bred for hunting rabbits in Spain, this sighthound is a remarkable combination of grace, agility, and endurance. Whether as a working dog or a loyal companion, the Ibizan Hound brings a unique charm and playful energy to any home.
Size: Medium to Large Weight: 45-65 lbs Lifespan: 11-14 years Temperament: Intelligent, Playful, Affectionate Coat: Short or wire-haired Exercise Needs: High Group: Hound

The Ibizan Hound has an ancient lineage, tracing back thousands of years to Egypt before being brought to the Balearic Islands of Spain. These dogs were bred for hunting small game and have remained relatively unchanged over centuries.  One of the oldest dog breeds, with origins in ancient Egypt.  Developed in Spain for rabbit hunting.  Known for its incredible speed and jumping ability.

The Ibizan Hound is sleek and agile, with a distinctive appearance that sets it apart.  A lean, athletic frame built for speed and endurance.  Large, upright ears that enhance their keen sense of hearing.  A long, narrow head with an alert and intelligent expression.  Short, smooth, or wire-haired coat that is easy to maintain.  Incredible jumping ability, often clearing high fences with ease.

The Ibizan Hound is affectionate, intelligent, and highly energetic. This breed forms strong bonds with its family and is known for its playful and friendly nature.  Gentle and affectionate: Loves being around family and enjoys human companionship.  Highly intelligent: Quick learner with a strong problem-solving ability.  Playful and energetic: Thrives in an active environment with plenty of stimulation.  Alert and watchful: Naturally cautious around strangers but not aggressive.

The Ibizan Hound is a highly active breed that requires ample exercise to stay healthy and happy. They excel in agility and lure coursing events.  Daily long walks or runs to meet their high energy levels.  Secure fencing is a must, as they can easily jump high barriers.  Training should be consistent, using positive reinforcement techniques.  Engage in scent games, lure coursing, or fetch to keep them mentally stimulated.

The Ibizan Hound has a low-maintenance coat, but regular grooming is still necessary.  Brush weekly to remove dirt and loose hair.  Bathe occasionally as needed to keep the coat clean.  Check ears regularly and clean them to prevent infections.  Trim nails and brush teeth for overall hygiene.

The Ibizan Hound is generally a healthy breed but may be prone to certain conditions.  Hip Dysplasia: A common joint issue in active breeds.  Bloat (Gastric Torsion): A life-threatening condition that requires immediate attention.  Deafness: Some Ibizan Hounds may have congenital hearing issues.  Eye Problems: Regular check-ups help maintain good vision health.

sections.section: Pros and  Cons of Owning an Ibizan Hound

sections.content: Friendly and affectionate, great for families.  Low-maintenance grooming needs.  Intelligent and trainable with proper guidance.  Playful and energetic, excelling in agility and sports.  Loyal and bonds strongly with its owners.

Requires significant exercise and space to run.  Strong prey drive makes them prone to chasing small animals.  Can be independent and stubborn if not trained early.  High jumping ability requires secure fencing.  Can be shy with strangers if not properly socialized.
